content: Bill Goldberg, MSW, LCSW, is a licensed clinical social worker and researcher specializing in the study of cults. He operates a private practice where he provides counseling to families of individuals involved in cults. Additionally, he is employed by the Rockland County Department of Mental Health in New York, where he oversees three outpatient mental health programs. Goldberg has been called upon to provide expert testimony before various state legislatures on topics such as regulations affecting residents of adult homes and issues related to cults. Specifically, he has testified before the New York State Assembly Committee on Child Care, the New York State Social Service Committee, the New Jersey State Assembly Judiciary Committee, and the Connecticut State Judiciary Committee. He has also appeared as an expert commentator on several prominent media platforms, including ABC News, The Sally Jesse Raphael Show, The John McLaughlin Show, MSNBC, and The Geraldo Rivera Show. For over 25 years, Goldberg and his wife, Lorna Goldberg, have co-facilitated a support group for former cult members. In recognition of their work, the couple was awarded the Leo J. Ryan Award in 1999 by the Leo J. Ryan Education Foundation. Together, they authored the article Group Work with Former Cultists, which was published in the journal Social Work. This article has been cited in numerous academic publications by notable scholars such as Louis Jolyon West, MD, Doni P. Whitsett, Michael Langone, PhD, and John Gordon Clark, MD. Education Goldberg became a Licensed Clinical Social Worker in New Jersey in 1995. He earned the designation of Board Certified Diplomate in Clinical Social Work from the American Board of Examiners in Clinical Social Work in 1988. He was certified as a Social Worker in New York in 1976. He received certification from the Academy of Certified Social Workers in 1972. Goldberg completed his Master of Social Work (MSW) degree at New York University in 1970. He earned his Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree from Rutgers University in 1968. Awards and Honors Goldberg received the Hall of Fame Award from the original Cult Awareness Network. He was honored with the Leo J. Ryan Award in 1999. Publications Books Goldberg contributed a chapter titled Guidelines for Support Groups to the book Recovery from Cults, edited by Michael Langone, PhD, and published by W.W. Norton and Company.
